newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK SAYS PLANS TALKS ON LIFTING MKT LIMITS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK SAYS PLANS TALKS ON LIFTING MKT LIMITS.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) on Friday said it planned to lift restrictions on non-residents participating in the local money market after a meeting with top officials at local banks on Tuesday.
"The limitations on entry of non-residents on our money market, which was established by agreement between the CNB and domestic banks, will be lifted," a CNB statement said.

"This will happen at the beginning of next week after a meeting of the CNB with representatives of commercial banks where the further functioning of the money and foreign exchange markets will be commonly considered," it added.
The statement gave no further details.

The CNB limited non-resident access to the local money market last month, as part of a series of measures aimed at easing downward pressure on the crown after a wave of short-selling pushed the currency to record lows.
CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters that it was the central bank's intention to remove the limits, but only after the talks with local banks.
"I think this is mainly according to the development on the market. The intention is to bring stability. These are gradual steps towards this," he said.
